passage: Beta, I am Pema, and my first trip alone was at fifteen, on the morning bus to Bua Rajni's town. It was excitement and fear in one stomach. We had agreed everything the night before: the bus number, the stops, the time I should reach, and that Bua Rajni would wait at the last stop with her phone on. On the bus I took out my ticket four times and counted the stops on my fingers each time. A woman in the next seat smiled at the ticket in my hand. When the last stop came, Bua Rajni was there, waving. I felt tall for the rest of the day.

qa.q: At what age did the narrator take the first trip alone?
qa.a: Pema took the first trip alone at fifteen.

qa.q: What was Pema feeling on the bus, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Pema felt excited and afraid at once, since the ticket came out four times and the stops were counted on the fingers.

qa.q: What had been agreed the night before that made the trip work?
qa.a: The bus number, the stops, the time of arrival, and that Bua Rajni would wait at the last stop with her phone on.

qa.q: How might Bua Rajni have felt waiting at the last stop?
qa.a: Bua Rajni was probably a little anxious while waiting and happy to see Pema arrive, waving from the stop.

grounding: Shows an elder recalling a teenager's first solo bus journey, excited and afraid, checking the ticket and stops with a route and contact agreed in advance.

passage: The announcement crackled and said Platform 4. Sarita, sixteen, was on her first solo train to her cousin's, and the platform had just changed. She checked her ticket, the display board and the announcement, and they agreed. Her heart was thumping. She had promised Parul she would text at every stop. She typed, "Platform changed to 4, I'm going there now," and climbed the stairs with the crowd. On the train she found her seat, put her bag on her lap and texted again. Parul replied in a minute: "Good. I'll be at the exit." Sarita breathed out and looked out of the window.

qa.q: Which platform was announced?
qa.a: Platform 4 was announced.

qa.q: What was Sarita feeling when the platform changed, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Sarita felt nervous, since her heart was thumping, but she checked the ticket, board and announcement before moving.

qa.q: What steps did Sarita follow that made her trip safer?
qa.a: She checked three sources, texted Parul at each stop, kept her bag on her lap and knew where Parul would be waiting.

qa.q: How might Parul have felt getting the messages?
qa.a: Parul was probably reassured to hear from Sarita at each stop, and glad to be ready at the exit.

grounding: Shows a teenager on a first solo train feeling excited and a little afraid, checking the platform and staying in contact with an agreed person.

passage:
Dear Diary, Saturday!!
My first bus trip ALONE. Pune to Satara to stay with Ritu Masi. Papa put me on the 8 o'clock bus and made me promise to message at every big stop. Masi knew the bus number and was going to meet me at the stand.
I checked my ticket about fifteen times. Seat 23. Seat 23. I kept looking at every signboard in case I missed Satara. At the food stop I was too nervous to get off, so I ate my packed paratha on the bus.
When I saw Masi waving at the stand, I felt SO grown up. And a bit shaky. 😅
Next time I'll get off at the food stop.
Vinita

qa.q: What was Vinita's seat number?
qa.a: Seat 23.

qa.q: How did Vinita feel on arriving at the stand?
qa.a: Vinita felt proud and grown up, and a bit shaky from the nervousness.

qa.q: What arrangements made this first solo trip safer?
qa.a: Papa and Masi agreed on the bus and meeting point, and Vinita messaged at every big stop.

qa.q: How might Ritu Masi have felt waiting at the stand?
qa.a: Ritu Masi was probably a little anxious and then happy and relieved to see Vinita arrive safely.

grounding: A teenager's diary shows the excitement and nerves of a first solo bus trip, made safe by an agreed route and contact.

passage: Zeenat, fourteen, had never taken the bus from her village near Aligarh to the town without an adult. Today she had to reach her aunt Devika's house for a week of tuition. Ammi had walked the route with her twice and written Devika Khala's number on the back of her hand as well as in her bag. At the stop, Zeenat checked the bus number against her paper, then again. On the bus, she counted each stop on her fingers, watching the sugar mill go by, then the petrol pump. When the clock tower appeared, she stood up too early and had to wait by the door, her heart thudding. Khala was at the stop. Zeenat grinned all the way to the house.

qa.q: Where was the number written besides her bag?
qa.a: On the back of her hand.

qa.q: What was Zeenat feeling as she waited by the door?
qa.a: She felt nervous and excited, her heart thudding, eager not to miss her stop.

qa.q: What preparation made Zeenat's first solo trip safe?
qa.a: Ammi walked the route with her twice and wrote down Khala's number, and Khala was waiting at the stop.

qa.q: How might Devika Khala feel seeing Zeenat step off the bus?
qa.a: Devika Khala would likely feel relieved and pleased to see her arrive safely and proudly.

grounding: Shows a teenager's first solo bus trip, checking the number and stops repeatedly, made safe by an agreed route and contact.

passage: Esther had checked her ticket five times before the Galway bus even left Dublin. Seat 14, window. Mum had written the plan on a card in her jacket pocket: text at Athlone, text at Ballinasloe, Uncle Javier waiting at Galway bus station, call him if anything changes. She was fourteen and had never gone this far alone. For the first hour she mostly watched the green fields slide past, grinning at nothing. Then the driver announced a twenty-minute delay for roadworks, and her stomach dropped. Would Javier leave? She read the card again, then texted: "Delay 20 min, still on bus, all ok." He replied at once: "No rush. I'll get a coffee 🙂" At Ballinasloe she checked the ticket again, just in case. When the bus finally pulled in, Javier stood by the door holding a sign that said ESTHER in huge letters, and she pretended to be embarrassed.

qa.q: Where did Mum's card say Esther should send texts?
qa.a: At Athlone and at Ballinasloe.

qa.q: How did Esther feel when the delay was announced?
qa.a: Her excitement turned to worry; her stomach dropped and she feared Javier might leave.

qa.q: What made the trip manageable for a first solo journey?
qa.a: The route and a contact person were agreed on the card, so when the delay came Esther knew exactly what to do: text Javier.

qa.q: How might Uncle Javier feel waiting at the bus station?
qa.a: Javier seems relaxed and proud, calm about the delay and playful with the big sign to welcome her.

grounding: Shows a teenager on a first solo journey, excited and a little afraid, kept steady by an agreed route and a contact person.
